Kimberly / team — see initial technical read below. I tried to keep recommendations conservative given the burst profile and regulatory overhead.

Summary recommendation (short):
- For pilot: 8 x A10G-equivalent GPUs in Dedicated (reserved burst pool) with autoscale to 16 GPUs for bursts using a warm pool. This gives headroom for 150 QPS steady, and handles ~450 QPS bursts with batching and aggressive prefix caching.
- For Private (VPC/on-prem): plan on ~20% compute uplift vs Dedicated due to network/IO and additional isolation overhead; recommend 10 x H100-equivalent for steady state with ability to scale to 24 for bursts if they require on-prem latency parity.

Technical rationale and details:
- Model & kernels: assume a 7B–13B family model (customer expects higher throughput). For 13B quantized to int8, an A10G-equivalent provides ~1.2x throughput vs older T4s; H100s are preferred on private if they need lower latency for long-form stateful chat.
- Batching & latency: continuous dynamic batching + prefix KV cache will reduce tokens/sec by ~25% effective at steady-state for repeat prompts. Suggest a 3-tier cache: per-request KV, tenant prefix cache, and global recurrent prompt cache.
- Concurrency math (rough):
  • Steady: 150 QPS * avg 40 tokens = 6k tokens/sec -> baseline 8 A10G-equivalents (~0.75 utilization target).
  • Burst headroom: 450 QPS -> require autoscale to ~16 GPUs or use burst fallback to slightly smaller model variant for short window.
- Network and isolation: Private on-prem adds 10–25% overhead depending on storage latency and size of KV caches. If they insist on strict tenant isolation (air-gapped), plan for additional warm pool sizing and longer provisioning lead times (2–6 weeks for on-prem equipment + config).
- Quantization & quality: recommend int8 for most gen traffic; keep a quantized fp16 path for quality-sensitive endpoints.

Operational suggestions:
- Canary path: start with Dedicated reserved 3-month pilot (8 GPUs) + 4-week performance runbook to validate latencies and cache-hit assumptions.
- Fallback policy: primary endpoint -> scaled dedicated pool -> lower-cost variant model (smaller quantized) in another region.

Open questions I need from Starthrive:
1) Distribution of prompt lengths (percentiles) and fraction of multi-turn sessions.
2) Whether encryption keys are customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for Private.
3) Expected retention for cache and KV storage sizes.

I'll draft a one-page sizing table once they provide the histograms.

- Aditya

Team / Tasha — looping back with commercial options and a recommended path that minimizes procurement friction while preserving an on-ramp to Private.

Three commercial paths (pricing bands are illustrative):
1) Pilot Reserved Pack (Low commitment): 3-month pilot, 8 A10G-equivalent GPUs, $45k/month. Includes 4-weeks performance validation and priority onboarding. Pilot transitions to Dedicated or converts credit toward Private if they sign a 12mo Private contract within 90 days.

2) Committed Dedicated (12/36mo): 12-month commit: baseline 8 GPUs reserved + burst to 16 (autoscale), $35k/month with volume discounts; 36-month: $28k/month. Includes SOC evidence package and standard SLAs. Change control for model variants allowed quarterly.

3) Private deployment uplift: one-time onboarding + infra delta + managed ops. Estimated uplift: 35–60% on top of base Dedicated pricing depending on rack configuration (H100 vs A100), KMS/HSM integration, and on-prem engineering. Lead time: 6–10 weeks from PO for cloud-hosted VPC private; 10–14+ weeks for fully air-gapped on-prem procurement and install.
